title: Three Years and One Short Lamp
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：sort　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sort 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the grandmother ① made the sort that no child in the courtyard would have described, and he said the making was the whole of the year. The ② sort, meaning the kind itself and not the lamp, ran three years and stayed undescribed in the book; a sort, he said, is the only thing in a courtyard that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ sort in that courtyard had the same short lamp beside it, and the ④ sort at the far window, meaning the gift they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A sort, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the grandmother said the describing is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the sort was the whole of the matter, meaning the order and not the kind. The ⑥ sort, meaning the order and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; sort, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a kind and an order. He said the order is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ sort had become a line in a diary, and the diary had become an argument about the short lamp. The ⑧ sort of the whole thing, the grandmother wrote in February, was one courtyard and three years of describing; sort, he said, is either the gift at the far window or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ sort I remember is the kind described in the diary, which closed in 1965 and is still described as the quietest in the courtyard. A ⑩ sort, my mother said in 1967, is the only kind that improves by being described; every sort, she said, is an order that has agreed to look like a kind. She said the order was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 种类；类别（指院子里每一种旁边的那一种）
B. n. 种类；类别（指那种种类本身，与小小的灯相对）
C. 固定搭配：make the sort 分出这一种种类
D. n. 种类；类别（指留给孩子们守着的那一件）
E. n. 种类之事（抽象总称，指一处院子的种类之事）
F. n. 种类；类别（指日记里写到、被描述的那一种）
G. n. 种类、条理（指一件事里人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 条理（抽象总称，指人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: made the sort that no child in the courtyard would have described
The sort, meaning the kind itself and not the lamp
the sort at the far window
the sort was the whole of the matter
the sort had become a line in a diary
The sort of the whole thing
A sort, my mother said in 1967

answers.why: make the sort 意为“分出这一种种类”，1958 年那位祖母把院子里没有一位孩子肯描述的一种种类做了一遍。
sort 意为“种类；类别”，指那种种类本身而不是小小的灯，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被描述。
sort 意为“种类；类别”，指院子里每一种旁边的那一种，每一种旁边都有同一盏小小的灯。
sort 意为“种类；类别”，指最远那扇窗边的留给孩子们守着的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
sort 意为“种类、条理”，指一件事里人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这种条理就是那件事的全部。
sort 意为“条理”，指人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西而不是那种种类，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
sort 意为“种类；类别”，指日记里写到、被描述的那一种，到 1963 年这一种成了日记里的一行。
sort 意为“种类之事”，祖母二月写道，整件事的种类之事是一处院子和三个年头的描述。
sort 意为“种类；类别”，我记得的是日记里描述过的那一种，1965 年过完了，至今仍被说成院子里最安静的一种。
sort 为抽象总称，母亲 1967 年说，种类是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的种类。
